name: Layered hair

card.summary: A haircut with sections cut at different lengths that adds volume, texture and movement, used to frame the face and change how hair sits.

quick.overview:
Layered hair is a cutting technique where sections are cut to different lengths and elevations so they overlap. The result adds texture, movement and shape while keeping overall length.

It improves looks by giving fine or flat hair more volume, removing bulk from thick hair, and framing the face. Styles range from 1970s feathered cuts to the 2020s wolf cut and butterfly cut.
quick.how: A stylist cuts hair at varying lengths, often with shorter layers on top or around the face. Cuts are adapted to hair type: dry cutting is used on curls, and floating layers on long straight hair.
quick.risks: Layers need regrowth and can need styling to look intended. Cutting too short a layer cannot be undone until it grows out.

lead: Layered hair is a haircutting technique in which sections are cut at different lengths and elevations to make overlapping layers, adding texture, movement and dimension while preserving overall length.[1] It contrasts with one-length or blunt cuts.[1]

The technique emerged in the late 1960s and spread through 1970s feathered looks such as Farrah Fawcett's, followed by the structured 1990s cuts like Jennifer Aniston's Rachel haircut.[1] Recent variants include the wolf cut (revived from 2022) and the butterfly cut with short face-framing layers over longer lengths.[1]
Benefits cited are more volume for fine hair, less weight in thick hair, easier styling and a graceful grow-out.[1]

chain: Weight removed or added where wanted
Fuller, more dynamic hair that frames the face
angle.text: Layers change the silhouette of hair, building volume on top or lightening ends, and face-framing pieces draw attention to features.

infobox: Feathered, wolf cut, butterfly, floating layers

paras: Layers are produced by elevating and overdirecting hair, roughly 90 degrees for shorter layers and 180 degrees for longer, graduated ones, to remove weight and encourage natural flow.[1]
Feathered layers, the Rachel cut, floating layers, wolf cut and butterfly cut are described as popular versions, tailored to hair type and lifestyle.[1]

timeline.event: Feathered layers popularised, for example by Farrah Fawcett.[1]
